text:
Predicates:
Hosted(x, y) ::: x hosted y.
Olympics(x) ::: x is an Olympics event.
SummerOlympics(x) ::: x is a Summer Olympics.
WinterOlympics(x) ::: x is a Winter Olympics.
Location(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
University(x) ::: x is a university.
RankedAmongBest(x) ::: x is ranked among the best universities.
City(x) ::: x is a city.
CapitalOf(x, y) ::: x is the capital of y.
PopulousCountry(x) ::: x is a populous country.
Region(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Games(x, y) ::: x hosted y.
NumberOfUniversities(x, y) ::: x has y universities.

Premises:
City(beijing) ∧ CapitalOf(beijing, people's_republic_of_china) ::: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.
City(beijing) ∧ CapitalOf(beijing, world's_most_populous_nation) ::: Beijing is the capital city of the world's most populous nation.
City(beijing) ∧ Region(beijing, northern_china) ::: Beijing is located in Northern China.
City(beijing) ∧ Games(beijing, summer_2008_olympics) ∧ Games(beijing, summer_2008_paralympics) ::: Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and Paralympics.
City(beijing) ∧ Hosted(beijing, summer_olympics_2008) ∧ Hosted(beijing, winter_olympics_2008) ::: Beijing has hosted the Summer and Winter Olympics.
City(beijing) ∧ Hosted(beijing, summer_olympics) ∧ Hosted(beijing, winter_olympics) ::: Beijing has hosted the Summer and Winter Olympics.
City(beijing) ∧ HasUniversities(beijing, 91) ∧ ∀x (University(x) ∧ InCity(x, beijing) → RankedAmongBest(x)) ::: Many of Beijing's 91 universities consistently rank among the best universities in the world.

Conclusion:
Hosted(beijing, summer_olympics_2008) ∧ Hosted(beijing, winter_olympics_2008) ::: Beijing hosted both the 2008 Summer Olympics and the Winter Olympics.
